phase6_visual_recovery.finding: ARKI had already produced materially developed architectural visual proposals across multiple scales, including high-rise/twin-tower concepts, residential, institutional/campus, bridge/infrastructure, pavilion and object/sculptural concepts.
phase6_visual_recovery.correction_to_previous_assumption: The historical weakness was not absence of architectural generation. The critical discontinuity was representation: 2D outputs could remain generic/schematic and fail to faithfully represent the architecture expressed in 3D/rendered proposals.
phase6_visual_recovery.observed_example: Double-helix twin-tower proposal: rendered massing/facade/bridges and spatial character are substantially richer than the accompanying conceptual Level 20 plan, which is diagrammatic and does not encode the same architectural specificity.
phase6_visual_recovery.phase6_problem_statement: Close the semantic-geometric-documentary loop so one canonical design state generates mutually consistent 3D geometry, plans, sections, elevations, program/topology, metrics and evidence rather than independent schematic representations.
truth_boundary: User-provided images are evidence of prior ARKI visual design output.
They do not by themselves prove canonical parametric geometry, structural feasibility, regulatory compliance, BIM completeness or executable documentation.
Do not downgrade these prior outputs to generic demo candidates; recover their generation lineage before replacing or reimplementing them.
next_recovery_actions: Locate the code, prompts/contracts, artifacts and checkpoints that generated these prior visual proposals.
Trace the 2D representation pipeline and identify where design-specific geometry/topology was lost.
Use a recovered high-rise case as Phase 6 regression specimen: 3D -> canonical state -> plan/section/elevation must preserve identity and relationships.
Integrate recovered specimens into the Design Testbed as historical benchmark cases, distinct from synthetic demo candidates.
